questions.q: Why are farmers increasingly turning to automation and IoT?
options: Labour is one of their largest costs
Machines sort fruit better while harvesting
It removes the need for any sorting
questions.explain: Automation cuts labour costs, though machine harvesting loses the chance to sort produce as it is picked.
questions.evidence: One of the largest costs is labor, so farmers are increasingly turning to automation and tools like IoT to reduce their labor costs.

questions.q: What is lost when produce is harvested by machine instead of by hand?
options: The ability to harvest at night
The ability to pick fruit from trees
The ability to sort food as it is being harvested
questions.explain: That is why image classifiers that spot unripe or damaged fruit are useful later in sorting lines.
questions.evidence: the ability to sort food as it is being harvested

questions.q: How does an object detector differ from an image classifier?
options: It gives one probability for the whole image
It only works on video, never on photos
It finds objects and where they are in the image
It needs no labelled training images
questions.explain: Classification scores the image as a whole; detection locates each object with a bounding box.
questions.evidence: These models don't classify an image by tags, instead they are trained to recognize objects, and can find them in images
